evidence.claim: Big Sheep Creek Back Country Byway runs for more than 50 miles through southwestern Montana, moving from the narrow rock walls of Big Sheep Canyon into broad valley country.
evidence.quote: Stretching more than 50 miles, the route is usually passable for all types of vehicles during the summer.

evidence.claim: BLM suggests three hours for the drive.
evidence.quote: Plan for a relaxing three-hour drive

evidence.claim: Most of the route is two-lane gravel; Visit Montana describes a short section of one-lane dirt.
evidence.quote: The 50 mile two-lane gravel road with a short stretch of one-lane dirt surface

evidence.claim: BLM highlights the canyon, a valley framed by mountains along the Continental Divide, and the winding Medicine Lodge valley farther north.
evidence.quote: the narrow, rocky walls of Big Sheep Canyon, a broad valley framed by mountains along the Continental Divide, and — farther north — the lush, winding Medicine Lodge valley

evidence.claim: The route became a Type I BLM Back Country Byway in 1989.
evidence.quote: The Big Sheep Creek BCB is designated as a Type I BLM Back Country Byway , established in 1989.

evidence.claim: Its designation promotes scenic, recreational and educational travel with minimal infrastructure, consistent with BLM’s backcountry preservation goals.
evidence.quote: The byway supports minimal infrastructure while promoting scenic, recreational, and educational experiences consistent with backcountry preservation goals.

evidence.claim: BLM says the road’s type has remained unchanged since that designation.
evidence.quote: The route remains unchanged in type since its original designation

evidence.claim: From Dell, leave I-15 for Westside Frontage Road, then join Big Sheep Creek Road at the beginning of the byway.
evidence.quote: To explore the Big Sheep Creek Back Country Byway from the south, start at the Dell Interchange on Interstate 15. Turn south onto Westside Frontage Road and travel about 2 miles until you reach Big Sheep Creek Road, which also marks the beginning of the Byway.

evidence.claim: The route passes Deadwood Campground before reaching Medicine Lodge Road.
evidence.quote: From the campground, follow the Big Sheep Creek Back Country Byway for nearly 12 miles until you come to Medicine Lodge Road, where the Byway continues.

evidence.claim: Turn north through the Medicine Lodge valley to Highway 324, just west of Clark Canyon Reservoir.
evidence.quote: Turn north onto Medicine Lodge Road and travel roughly 30 miles until you reach Highway 324, just west of Clark Canyon Reservoir.

evidence.quote: Dell was founded as a station stop on the newly completed Utah and Northern Railway, which reached Butte in 1881. It became a trading center for ranchers.
